title: Fit check pins with a go no-go gauge plate
instruction: Gauge the six grey pins. Seat every pin that drops fully into a gauge pocket and put every pin that does not fit on the red reject pad.
context: Receiving inspection of flight pins and fasteners before spacecraft integration, a ground job done in 1 g exactly as here. The pins differ by 8 mm in diameter, so a careful eye can sort them, but the gauge plate is the arbiter: an oversize pin cannot enter a pocket, and the score nets every misrouted pin, so neither guessing nor dumping every pin on one destination earns credit. Unlike two-way size sorts into bins, the destination is decided by a fixed fit gauge, and a misrouted pin cancels a correct one.
setup: On the table in front of the left arm (x forward from the arm bases, y left). Fixed, dark grey (sRGB 0.25, 0.25, 0.27), matte: a gauge plate 25 mm tall with three square pockets 24 x 24 mm and 25 mm deep, open to the table, their centres 132, 176 and 220 mm in front of the base line and 105 mm inboard of the left arm's base, 44 mm apart; it is built from two side walls 152 x 5 x 25 mm and four cross walls 20 x 24 x 25 mm, footprint 152 x 34 mm. Fixed, red (sRGB 0.85, 0.12, 0.12), matte: a reject pad 120 x 80 x 5 mm centred 200 mm in front of the base line and 25 mm outboard of the left arm's base. Loose, light grey (sRGB 0.75, 0.75, 0.75), matte, all 60 mm tall and identical in finish: three go pins of 20 mm diameter, 30 g each, standing 310, 310 and 380 mm in front of the base line at 135 mm inboard, 65 mm outboard and 35 mm inboard of the left arm's base; three no-go pins of 28 mm diameter, 50 g each, standing at 310 mm in front and 35 mm inboard, 380 mm in front and 135 mm inboard, and 380 mm in front and 65 mm outboard. A go pin enters a pocket with 2 mm of clearance per side; a no-go pin cannot enter in any orientation and stands on the walls with its bottom 25 mm above the table. Pin centres are at least 70 mm apart, and the closest edges anywhere in the layout are 40 mm apart (the reject pad and the two nearest pins). The right arm is idle at its ready pose.
scoring: End state only, scored at the last control step; a pin counts only when at rest (moving under 10 mm/s). On the pad: bottom within 4 mm of the pad's top face and centre inside its 120 x 80 mm footprint, standing or lying. On the gauge: centre within 10 mm of the plate's 152 x 34 mm footprint and bottom more than 10 mm above the table (standing on the walls, lying across them, or propped on them); a pin leaning against the plate with its bottom on the table is neither. Correct: a 20 mm pin in a pocket (centre inside the 24 x 24 mm opening, bottom within 3 mm of the table) or a 28 mm pin on the pad. Wrong: a 20 mm pin on the pad or a 28 mm pin on the gauge. Neither: a pin anywhere else on the table, or off the table. Score = max(0, correct minus wrong) / 6, so 0, 0.17, 0.33, 0.5, 0.67, 0.83 or 1.0; success, which ends the trial, is 1.0 held for 1 s. All six pins on the pad scores 0 (three correct, three wrong); every pin pushed at the gauge scores 0; the three go pins seated with the rejects untouched scores 0.5. The plate and pad are fixed in simulation. Judging from a photo: pins in pockets are go by construction, pins on the walls are rejects left on the gauge, pins on the pad are checked for their centre inside the pad edge and measured with calipers (20 against 28 mm).
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the six pins back on their marks; the plate and pad do not move.
fidelity: Approximate: real go no-go gauges discriminate tenths of a millimetre; here the diameters differ by 8 mm against a 24 mm pocket because the simulator's 5 mm contact offset makes tighter fits unreliable, so a policy may sort by sight before it gauges. Square pockets stand in for round bores. Rigid primitives with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), matte colours, masses of 30 and 50 g as printed plastic would be. Earth gravity, which is also the real job's gravity. The simulated scorer cannot see the grippers; on the real rig the trial is judged after the arms withdraw, and a plate or pad moved more than 5 mm scores 0.
